blocks.text: Have you ever wondered how your body moves? The secret lies in the joints and muscles!

blocks.markdown: In mammals, joints and muscles work together to facilitate movement. Joints are the points where two or more bones meet, while muscles are responsible for the force that moves these bones. Understanding the types of joints and how muscles work is crucial in biology.

blocks.title: Definition of Joints
blocks.text: Joints are the connections between bones that allow for movement and flexibility in the skeleton.

blocks.markdown: Joints can be classified into three main types: **Immovable joints**, which do not allow any movement (e.g., skull bones); **Slightly movable joints**, which allow limited movement (e.g., joints between vertebrae); and **Freely movable joints**, which allow a wide range of movement (e.g., knee and elbow joints).

blocks.title: Identifying Joint Types
blocks.prompt: Classify the following joints: skull sutures, vertebral joints, and knee joints.
blocks.answer: Skull sutures: Immovable, Vertebral joints: Slightly movable, Knee joints: Freely movable.

blocks.markdown: Next, let's explore synovial joints, which are the most common type of joint in the body. A synovial joint is characterized by a joint capsule, synovial fluid, cartilage, and ligaments. The joint capsule surrounds the joint and contains synovial fluid, which lubricates the joint.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Remember to describe the parts of a synovial joint and their functions, as this is a common exam question.

blocks.markdown: Movement at the elbow is a great example of how muscles work in pairs. The biceps and triceps are antagonistic muscles; when one contracts, the other relaxes. When you lift your arm, the biceps contract and the triceps relax, allowing for movement.

blocks.title: Key Point
blocks.text: Antagonistic muscles work in opposition to produce movement. The biceps flex the arm, while the triceps extend it.

points: Joints can be classified as immovable, slightly movable, or freely movable.
Synovial joints are characterized by a joint capsule, synovial fluid, cartilage, and ligaments.
Antagonistic muscles, like the biceps and triceps, work together to produce movement.
